A PYMNTS report found that 70% of restaurant patrons consider waiting to pay the most frustrating aspect of their dining experience. Restaurant payment systems like mobile ordering and self-service kiosks significantly reduce wait times, leading to faster service and happier customers.
There's a certain nostalgia about cash registers, but today they are one of the largest bottlenecks in quick restaurants. Here's why handheld point of sale is the future of restaurant payments:
Mobility Matters

Hand-held Point-of-purchase systems untether you from a fixed cash register. Imagine servers taking orders tableside, processing payment then and there, and without waiting for others. That translates into more efficient waiting, more content customers, and more tables turned.
Efficiency is the Key

Handheld point-of-sale systems streamline ordering and payment processing. They mostly come with intuitive interfaces and pre-programmed menus, so personnel can take orders easily and, in some cases, heap process them in easy steps.
Embrace the Power of Data

The hand-held point-of-sale devices are data powerhouses. They capture invaluable sales data, track inventory levels, and let you know, in real time, the performance of your business. Now you can make data-driven decisions regarding your menu prices, staffing arrangements, and promotional offers.
Lesser Mistakes, More Security

No more handwritten receipts and manual computation. A handheld point of sale system: digital order entries and secure payment processing eliminate error possibilities. In other words, both you and your customers will have enhanced accuracy and reduced risks from fraud.

Handheld point of sale lets you craft personal payment experiences with customers. Customers can pay right at the table, split their check by item or amount, redeem loyalty points, or even leave digital tips, all at a tap of the screen. This will increase overall customer satisfaction and repeat visits.
Choosing the Right Handheld Point of Sale for Your Restaurant
Abound with handheld point-of-sale systems, finding the best system for your restaurant might turn out to be a cumbersome task. Here are some key points you need to consider:
Features

The system should be user-friendly to your employees. It should also be easy to use to make it possible for your employees to navigate through it with ease. Ensure that the system contains features that are easy and intuitive and that it provides adequate training resources for your team.
Integration Capabilities
Make sure that the handheld point-of-sale is integrated with third-party applications such as accounting and online ordering software you may be using.
Scalability
Consider your expansion plans. Get a system that's going to grow with your business, accommodate more staff, and increase sales.
Cost
Handheld point-of-sale systems are available at price points, ranging from. Think of the features, scalability, and extra ongoing costs of support.

title: Culinary Innovations: Highlights from the National Restaurant Show
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Will people's preference for spicy and sweet food fade? Is there a decrease in plant-based meat?

body.text: Will people's preference for spicy and sweet food fade? Is there a decrease in plant-based meat?
A Comprehensive Walkthrough

Answers to these and a preview of future developments can be found at this year's annual National Restaurant Show. To bring you the major menu trends that we found, we visited a lot of exhibit aisles, went to a lot of training sessions, and tasted a lot of food both inside and outside of McCormick Place.

Energy drinks, fruity sodas, sparkling wines without alcohol, boba, coffee, tea, and a plethora of other liquid refreshments were available at the fair. But as we were searching for fresh drink flavors, cardamom began to rise.
Exploring The Emerging Flavours

A mandarin cardamom soft drink with a hint of turmeric was available from Tractor, a boutique beverage brand making inroads into the fast-casual market. At the California Milk Advisory Board pavilion, samples of cardamom mango lassi were distributed. The fragrant spice gives these drinks a nice, exotic twist, but it's also commonly used in baking and Indian food.
Fermentation And Umami Explosions

Food is preserved by fermentation, which also enhances umami, the savory fifth taste that is difficult to pinpoint. Planit POD, a novel fermentation system that Waring unveiled at its booth, is intended to ferment and pasteurize plant-based proteins like tempeh and koji in a mere 24 hours.
Chef Jeremy Umansky used mold fermentation to create a crispy, intensely flavorful crust on the proteins and to explode with flavor in his chickpea tempeh and Middle Eastern-spiced meat mixture.
Innovative Substitutes of Caviare

Although caviare has long been considered a delicacy for fine dining establishments, most operators find it to be neither sustainable nor cost-effective. There are a few products this year that, at least in terms of texture and presentation, can be substituted for caviar. Chile Pepper Flavor is one of the FABI award winners for food and beverage innovation. The caviar-sized pearls are naturally filled with a liquid mixture of chili and red bell peppers. When eaten, they release a delectable burst of flavor and make an eye-catching garnish.

Little pearls known as caviar oil, which are made from Arbequina olive oil, have a more neutral flavor and the same effect. We also sampled finger lime caviar, which is imported from Australia by Mad Honey. The fruit contains pearls, which can be purchased frozen. They can also be melted in the tongue to produce the "caviar effect" and a striking garnish of pastel hues.

Seaweed flakes can be used instead if you'd rather have a saltier, more caviar-like flavor. Ocean's Balance makes butter that resembles real caviar in both taste and appearance by combining seaweed flakes with lemon peel.
Unique Version of Pizza Crusts

Seaweed butter works well as a spread on bread. Pine nuts are a type of flatbread from Rome that's becoming popular as a pizza crust of the future. The one we sampled was hand-rolled, gluten-free, and maintained its crispy texture even when paired with cheese and veggies. It's better for you and easier to digest than regular pizza dough, which is helpful when you spend hours stuffing your face with samples from dozens of exhibitors.
Beverages Infused with THC

Many states allow the sale and service of THC-containing drinks, so exhibitors were open to moving from CBD vendors to those offering a stronger cannabis derivative. We tried a thimbleful of CannaSpritz from Flora Hemp Spirits. Even though it only has 3 milligrams of THC, we felt a little high. The drink's best feature is that it had a nice flavor profile: it was dry, bubbly, and slightly sweet with hints of floral notes.
Canna Spritz

The team at RB enjoyed Avocados from Mexico's Guacamole Bar, but we were particularly fond of the Guac Extensions made by Modern Market's chef Nate Weir, who conducted the demonstrations on Monday. To add some bitterness, he first mashed fresh avocado with tomatillo salsa as a base and then added hops, which is the same ingredient in beer. This guacamole gave a fish taco a complex flavor boost.
A Twist to Guacamole

Weir combined tamarind with avocado in the second demonstration to add tropical flavors that were both sweet and sour. They served it with glazed grilled shrimp and added some roasted mushrooms, tomatillo salsa, and a hint of spicy crunch. They intend to dispel the myth that guacamole is only appropriate for Mexican or Latin American cooking. For us, it was effective.
The Zero-Waste Spirits

The California dairy industry is pushing a new spirit called Wheyward Wheyskey, which is made from recycled whey leftover from making cheese. The beverage is served in a drink akin to an espresso martini and is topped with a scoop of double rainbow vanilla ice cream. The zero-waste trend served as the inspiration for this product. tasted rich and delicious, like a slightly alcoholic affogato.

This was all about the menu trends we found this year at the National Restaurant Show. Which trend would you like to try for yourself? The show was entertaining for the foodies and it surely created some future food trends.

What is a Customer Facing Display?

Before the nitty-gritty of choosing a display solution is explored, it should be cleared up what exactly a customer-facing display (CFD) is. Simply put, a CFD is a screen showing relevant information to customers. This could include anything from advertisements and promotions to transaction details and digital menus.

These displays are often found in retail stores, quick-service restaurants, hotels, and even healthcare facilities. They not only serve as an information tool but also as a medium for engaging and interacting with customers.
Benefits of Customer Facing Displays
The question might arise, “Is a CFD really needed for my business?” The short answer is yes, and here’s why:

1\. Enhanced Customer Experience: Real-time information such as itemized receipts, current promotions, and loyalty rewards are provided to customers by CFDs. This transparency leads to trust and improvement in the overall customer experience.

2\. Effective Marketing Tool: By displaying promotions and advertisements, customer purchasing decisions at the point of sale can be influenced by CFDs. The potential of showing a timely offer that prompts a last-minute purchase can be imagined!
3\. Reduced Perceived Wait Time: Entertaining or informative content on the display can make the waiting time seem shorter, keeping customers happy and engaged while they wait.

4\. Improved Operational Efficiency: These displays can assist in reducing errors by clearly showing transaction details to both customers and employees. A smoother checkout process and less confusion result from this.
Key Features to Look for in a Customer Facing Display

1\. High Resolution and Brightness: The display should be clear and easy to read. High resolution ensures that text and images are crisp, while adequate brightness makes it visible even in well-lit environments.

2\. Touchscreen Capabilities: Interactivity is a significant bonus. Engaging with the display is allowed for customers through a touchscreen, whether it’s through browsing digital catalogs or entering loyalty program details.

3\. Versatile Mounting Options: Depending on the business setup, wall-mounted, countertop, or even pole-mounted displays might be needed. Flexibility in mounting options ensures the display's positioning in the most effective spot for customer interaction.

4\. Robust Software Integration: Seamless integration with your point of sale (POS) system should be ensured for the display. The ability to update content remotely and in real-time is also a crucial feature, especially for dynamic promotional needs.

5\. Durability and Warranty: CFDs are typically a one-time investment, so longevity is essential. Displays that come with a good warranty and are built to withstand daily operational wear and tear should be looked for.
Types of Customers Facing Displays
Depending on the business type and specific needs, different kinds of CFDs are available:
1\. Standalone Displays: Used typically for advertisements and digital menus, these displays are not connected to the point-of-sale system and are mainly for informational or promotional purposes.

2\. Point of Sale Integrated Displays: Integrated directly with the point-of-sale system, these displays show real-time transaction details, pricing, and promotions. They are ideal for transparent customer interactions and efficient transaction handling.

3\. Interactive Kiosks: As larger, touchscreen-enabled displays, these serve as self-service stations. Handling everything from order placement to payment processing is possible, reducing the need for staff involvement.
How to Implement Customer Facing Displays Effectively
Having the right CFD is just part of the equation; effective implementation is where the magic happens. Some practical tips are:
1\. Strategic Placement: Positioning the display where it's most likely to catch the customers’ eyes is crucial. Countertops, near the checkout area, or in waiting zones are prime locations.
2\. Content is King: Relevance and engagement are paramount for the content displayed. Regular updates should be made to keep up with current promotions and seasonality.
3\. Train Your Staff: Comfort and troubleshooting capability for the CFD should be ensured for the employees. Proper training ensures they can assist customers effectively if any issues arise.
4\. Monitor and Adjust: Analytics, if available, should be used to monitor how customers interact with the display. Necessary adjustments should be made to keep the content effective and engaging.
Conclusion

Investment in a customer-facing display is a step towards the modernization of your business and the enhancement of the overall customer experience. By careful selection of the right type and features and ensuring effective implementation, a powerful tool for engagement and sales growth can be created from your CFD.

At the end of the day, the goal is to create a seamless, enjoyable experience for your customers, and a well-chosen customer-facing display can help you achieve just that. Shopping for your perfect display solution is wished to be happy!

body.text: Running a fast casual restaurant comes with its own unique set of challenges. Between managing a steady influx of customers, maintaining quality, and ensuring smooth operations, there's a lot on your plate, pun intended. That's where handheld point of sale (POS) technology steps in, offering efficiency at your fingertips. In this article, we’ll break down how handheld point of sale systems can revolutionize your fast casual restaurant, making it easier to manage orders, boost customer satisfaction, and keep your staff happy.
What Exactly is Handheld Point of Sale Technology for Fast Casual Restaurants?

First things first, let's talk about what handheld point of sale technology actually is. A handheld point of sale system is essentially a portable, miniaturized version of the traditional POS system but is optimized for mobility. Think of it as a high-tech notepad that takes orders, processes payments, and even helps track customer preferences, all from a single device. It’s like having a mini command center in your hand.
Speeding Up Order Taking
One of the biggest advantages of handheld point of sale systems is the speed they bring to order taking.
Reduced Wait Times

When servers can take orders directly at the table and send them instantly to the kitchen, it cuts down on the time customers have to wait. No more running back and forth to stationary terminals. Whether someone’s grabbing a quick lunch or meeting friends for a casual dinner, nobody likes waiting. Handheld point of sale systems ensure that orders are processed faster, meaning happier, and often more regular, customers.
Accuracy in Orders

With handheld point of sale, you can significantly reduce the chances of order errors. Because orders are entered directly into the system and sent to the kitchen, there’s less room for miscommunication. And let’s be honest, fewer errors mean fewer comped meals and happier customers.
Boosting Staff Productivity
When your staff spends less time running between tables and point of sale terminals, they can focus on providing excellent service.
More Face Time with Customers

Handheld point of sale systems allow servers to stay on the floor rather than darting back and forth to a fixed terminal. This means they can spend more time talking to customers, answering questions, and upselling menu items, all of which can lead to increased sales and better tips for the staff. Win-win!
Training Made Easy

Because handheld point of sale systems are often designed with intuitive, user-friendly interfaces, training new staff can be quicker and easier. With less time spent learning the system, new hires can focus on what they do best, delivering outstanding service.
Enhancing Customer Experience
In today’s competitive market, customer experience is king. Handheld point of sale systems can play a big role in enhancing that experience.
Convenient Payment Options

Customers appreciate payment flexibility. Handheld point of sale systems often support various payment methods, including credit/debit cards, mobile payments, and even contactless options like Apple Pay and Google Wallet. No more customers awkwardly passing around their cards; the whole process becomes smooth and swift.
Personalized Service

With integrated customer relationship management (CRM) features, handheld point of sale systems can track customer preferences and order history. This can enable your staff to provide a more personalized dining experience. Imagine a server greeting a regular customer with “Welcome back, would you like to order your usual?” These small touches can set your restaurant apart from the competition.
Streamlining Back-End Operations
It’s not just the front of house that benefits; handheld point of sale technology can revolutionize back-end operations too.
Real-Time Inventory Management

Many handheld point of sale systems come with integrated inventory management features, allowing you to track stock in real-time. This ensures that you always know what’s available, reducing waste and making inventory reorders more efficient.
Detailed Reporting

Handheld point of sale systems can generate detailed reports on sales, customer preferences, and even staff performance. This data can be invaluable for making informed decisions about everything from menu changes to staffing levels. Knowing what sells and when can help you optimize your menu and your operations to better meet customer demands.
Integrating Online and In-Store Operations
The foodservice landscape is shifting, and offering online orders and delivery options has become essential for many restaurants.
Seamless Integration

Handheld point of sale systems often come with features that easily integrate with your online ordering platforms. Orders placed online can be sent directly to the kitchen, just like in-store orders, ensuring a seamless operation. This means you can manage dine-in, takeaway, and delivery orders all from the same system.
Enhanced Communication

When your point of sale system is integrated with your delivery platforms, it ensures that everyone, from kitchen staff to delivery drivers, is on the same page. This can reduce errors, improve efficiency, and ensure a consistent customer experience across all platforms.
Future-Proofing Your Restaurant
Technology isn’t just about solving today’s problems; it’s about preparing for tomorrow’s challenges.
Scalability

Handheld point of sale systems are scalable, meaning they can grow with your business. Whether you’re expanding your menu, opening a new location, or simply handling increased customer demand, your point of sale system can adapt to your needs.
Regular Updates

Many handheld point of sale systems offer regular software updates, ensuring that you’re always equipped with the latest features and security measures. This can give you peace of mind, knowing that your system is up-to-date and that you’re staying ahead of the curve.
Conclusion and Next Steps

Handheld point of sale technology is more than just a trend; it’s a powerful tool that can help you improve efficiency, boost customer satisfaction, and streamline your operations. As the dining landscape continues to evolve, adopting this technology can set your fast casual restaurant apart from the competition.

title: Erika Flowers Leads at Compère Lapin, New Orleans - eatOS
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: The award-winning Caribbean and European-inspired restaurant Compère Lapin has gained recognition for its outstanding bar program and Chef Nina Compton's delectable dishes since its June 2015 opening. Compton and...

body.text: The award-winning Caribbean and European-inspired restaurant Compère Lapin has gained recognition for its outstanding bar program and Chef Nina Compton's delectable dishes since its June 2015 opening. Compton and husband/partner Larry Miller are happy to announce that Erika Flowers has been appointed as Compère Lapin's bar lead. This appointment took place this spring. A native of the Bronx with roots in Belize, Flowers will elevate the bar program and bring her love of creating inventive cocktails by emphasizing Caribbean-inspired beverages that go well with Chef Compton's hearty fare.
Meet Erika Flower: A Bronx Native With Belizean Roots

Larry Miller says, "We are ecstatic to welcome Erika to the Compere Lapin family." “Her passion for mixology and innovative approach to crafting cocktails align with our commitment to offering visitors an exceptional dining experience. We are confident that Erika will enhance Compère Lapin’s reputation as a destination for food and drink enthusiasts.”
Crafting Caribbean-Inspired Cocktails: Erika's Signature Style
Inspired by the vibrant cultures of the Caribbean and New Orleans, Flowers will present her distinctive style with a variety of seasonal drinks that highlight the tastes of the islands.

The following cocktails are sure to please guests: Honeymoon Phase, a spritz cocktail that combines your choice of Ketel One Vodka or Wonderbird Gin with strawberry peppercorn syrup, Cocchi Rosa, cava, and a splash of soda water for a refreshing and subtly floral experience; Sur-prise Me, a tropical-inspired cocktail that combines El Buho Espadin Mezcal, Paranubes Oaxacan Rum, and Braulio with lemon juice, cinnamon syrup, and crisp grapefruit soda; a sprinkle of Angostura bitters completes the dish.
From Turning Tables to Compère Lapin: Erika's Journey in Mixology

"I'm thrilled about the opportunity to work with beverage director Roxy Eve Narvaez and chef Nina Compton, two women I've long admired, to create a bar program that incorporates Caribbean flavors and inspiration from my travels, and to empower my bar team." My creations are always accompanied by a backstory, so it is a privilege for me to curate a menu at Compere Lapin that will enhance the tales presented through the food. It is a comprehensive experience, and I am excited to offer it to everyone who enters those doors as Erika puts it.

Erika, whose parents are from Belize, was born and raised in The Bronx, New York, and moved to New Orleans in August of 2008. Flowers didn't have any formal training when she started working in the cocktail industry in 2021. She was a member of the prestigious Turning Tables Bar Program Cohort III, a local nonprofit that aims to increase diversity in the hospitality industry through externship placement and training programs.

Erika transitioned gracefully from server to bartender thanks to the program. This crucial occasion allowed her to apply her newly acquired knowledge to Taste of the Tropics, her handmade product line, and immersive pop-up events honoring Caribbean heritage.
The Future of Cocktails: Erika's Influence and Certifications

Erika started her career in 2021 as a bartender at the internationally acclaimed cocktail bar Cane & Table. Erika committed herself to honing her skills and highlighting her Belizean heritage while she was there. With her expertise, she expertly crafted sugarcane spirits, adding unique flavors and bitters to them. The outcome was an assortment of unique cocktails that won her recognition and awards, including a spot on PUNCH: Best New Bartenders of 2023.

Nina Compton and Larry Miller hired Flowers in 2024 to be the bar lead for their flagship restaurant, located inside the Old No. 77 Hotel & Chandlery. She keeps pushing the envelope at Compère Lapin by creating inventive cocktails and guiding her staff with style and grace. Erika is certified by the Bar 5-Day program, WSET Level 2 in Spirits, and numerous other brands, which have given her the chance to perform live across the country.

title: Honoring the Pillars of Progress: Celebrating National Labor Day
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: National Labor Day is much more than just a long weekend or a well-deserved break from the hustle and bustle of our daily routines. It stands as an enduring tribute to the countless men and women who have contributed to...

body.text: National Labor Day is much more than just a long weekend or a well-deserved break from the hustle and bustle of our daily routines. It stands as an enduring tribute to the countless men and women who have contributed to the socio-economic fabric of our nation. By setting aside this special day, we recognize and appreciate the hard work, dedication, and tenacity of the labor force. This year, as we gather to observe this holiday, let's delve deeper into the origins, significance, and contemporary relevance of National Labor Day.
The Origins of Labor Day

Labor Day originated in the late 19th century during a time when the Industrial Revolution was at its peak. Working conditions were often grueling and hazardous, with laborers enduring long hours for minimal pay. Amid these challenging conditions, labor unions began to organize, advocating for better wages, reasonable working hours, and improved workplace safety standards.

The first Labor Day parade took place on September 5, 1882, in New York City, where approximately 10,000 workers marched in solidarity for their rights. This movement quickly gained momentum, leading to the establishment of the first official Labor Day holiday in the state of Oregon on February 21, 1887. Soon after, other states followed suit, and in 1894, President Grover Cleveland signed into law the bill that made Labor Day a national holiday.
The Achievements of Labor Movements

Labor movements have been instrumental in shaping the modern workplace. From reducing work hours and abolishing child labor to securing health benefits and promoting workplace safety, the impact of these movements is far-reaching. Notable milestones include:

items: The 8-Hour Workday: The fight for an 8-hour workday was a pivotal battle for labor unions. The slogan "Eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, and eight hours for what we will" became synonymous with labor rights.
The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA): Enacted in 1938, the FLSA established minimum wage, overtime pay, and prohibited the employment of minors in oppressive child labor.

Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA): Passed in 1970, OSHA aimed to ensure safe and healthful working conditions for every worker by setting and enforcing standards and providing training, education, and assistance.

body.text: Celebrating Modern Workers

Today, National Labor Day serves as a reminder of how vital workers are to the nation’s ongoing success. From healthcare professionals, educators, and frontline workers to engineers, artists, and manual laborers, each profession contributes uniquely to our collective well-being.
The Role of Diversity and Inclusion in the Workforce

One of the most significant transformations in the labor landscape has been the push towards diversity and inclusion. Recognizing the strength that a diverse workforce brings, organizations are putting concerted efforts into creating inclusive work environments where every individual has the opportunity to thrive.
Workforce Trends: Adapting to a Digital Age

The digital revolution has introduced a new paradigm in the way we work. Automation, artificial intelligence, and telecommuting are reshaping industries across the board. While these technological advancements offer numerous benefits, they also present challenges such as job displacement and the need for continuous skill development. Embracing lifelong learning and adaptable skill sets will be crucial for workers to stay relevant in this evolving landscape.
The Importance of Worker Rights and Advocacy
Despite considerable progress, the quest for equitable treatment and safe working conditions continues. Labor unions, advocacy groups, and policies must remain vigilant in protecting workers’ rights.
How to Participate in Labor Day
There are many ways to honor and celebrate Labor Day:

items: Join a Parade or Rally: Participate in local events to show solidarity with workers.
Support Local Businesses: Shop locally to support community workers and small businesses.
Educational Initiatives: Host or attend talks and workshops focused on labor history, workers’ rights, and current labor issues.
Volunteer: Engage in community service projects to give back and support local workers.

body.text: Looking Ahead: The Future of Labor

As we look towards the future, it's essential to build on the achievements of the past while addressing present and emerging challenges. Promoting workplace innovation, supporting mental health, and ensuring fair wages will be integral to sustaining a robust labor force.
Conclusion

National Labor Day is a celebration of the grit, determination, and indispensable contributions of workers across all sectors. Their relentless efforts have not only built our cities and industries but have also laid the foundation for future generations. As we commemorate this day, let us pledge to support and advance the rights and well-being of every worker, ensuring that their invaluable contributions continue to propel our nation forward.
Happy National Labor Day!

body.text: Restaurant owners and managers are continually challenged to find new ways to streamline operations, elevate customer experiences, and increase profitability, all while maintaining the human touch that keeps guests coming back. What is Restaurant Technology Cloud?

These tools cover various facets of restaurant management, including but not limited to inventory management, employee scheduling, point of sale system (POS) systems, and customer relationship management (CRM).
Streamlining Inventory Management

One of the primary pain points for many restaurateurs is inventory management. Running out of ingredients during peak hours can be disastrous, while overstocking can lead to waste and increased costs. Cloud-based inventory systems offer real-time tracking and automatic restocking alerts.
Real-time Tracking

With cloud technology, you can monitor inventory levels across multiple locations in real-time. This means you'll always know when you’re running low on essential items and can reorder proactively. Cloud-based point of sale systems support a wide array of payment options, including credit cards, mobile payments, and even cryptocurrencies. This flexibility ensures that you can cater to the payment preferences of all your customers.
Data Analytics

One of the most powerful features of cloud-based point of sale systems is their ability to generate detailed reports. You can track sales trends, menu item popularity, and customer preferences, helping you make data-driven decisions to optimize your menu and marketing strategies.
Improving Customer Relationship Management
In the competitive restaurant industry, building and maintaining strong customer relationships is vital. Cloud-based CRM systems help you understand and interact with your customers more effectively.

These systems automatically collect data on customer preferences, order history, and feedback. This information can be used to personalize marketing efforts, recommend dishes, and enhance the overall dining experience.
Loyalty Programs

Cloud-based CRM systems make it easy to implement and manage loyalty programs. Digital rewards can be tracked automatically, removing the hassle of punch cards or physical stamps. This encourages repeat business and builds customer loyalty.
Offering Online Ordering and Delivery

The demand for online ordering and delivery has surged, especially in light of recent global events. Cloud-based systems facilitate a seamless online ordering experience, ensuring your restaurant can cater to this growing market.
Easy Integration

These systems can easily integrate with third-party delivery services, such as Uber Eats and DoorDash. Orders are automatically routed to the kitchen, reducing the risk of errors and ensuring a smooth workflow.

Data security is a significant concern for any business, and restaurants are no exception. Cloud-based systems offer robust security features to protect sensitive information.

Advanced encryption and secure payment gateways ensure that customer payment information is protected, reducing the risk of fraud. Regular software updates also ensure that your systems are safeguarded against the latest threats.

With cloud technology, your data is automatically backed up and stored securely off-site. This provides peace of mind, knowing that your valuable information is safe from physical damage or cyber-attacks.

body.text: The quick service restaurant (QSR) industry has always been synonymous with speed and convenience, striving to deliver fast, efficient, and reliable service. In recent years, self-service kiosks have emerged as a transformative technology within the QSR sector. These intuitive and interactive devices enhance operational efficiency and elevate the customer experience. Let's explore how self-service kiosks are reshaping the landscape of quick service restaurants and why integrating them into your quick service restaurant software could be a game-changer.
Improving Operational Efficiency through Self-Service Kiosks
Reduced Wait Times

One of the primary benefits of self-service kiosks is their ability to handle large volumes of customers efficiently. By allowing customers to place their orders directly at kiosks, QSRs can significantly reduce wait times, especially during peak hours. Multiple kiosks can serve more customers simultaneously compared to a single cashier, ensuring faster service and higher customer turnover.
Optimized Labor Allocation

With self-service kiosks handling the bulk of the ordering process, employees can be redirected to other critical areas such as food preparation, order fulfillment, and customer service. This optimized labor allocation ensures better resource management and helps maintain the quality and speed of service.
Enhancing the Customer Experience
Personalized Ordering

Self-service kiosks offer a highly personalized ordering experience. Customers can take their time to browse the menu, customize their orders to their exact preferences, and avoid any potential miscommunication with cashiers. This personalization ensures that customers receive precisely what they want, enhancing their satisfaction and reducing the likelihood of errors.
User-Friendly Interfaces

Modern self-service kiosks are equipped with intuitive, user-friendly interfaces that make the ordering process straightforward and enjoyable. High-quality images, easy-to-navigate menus, and touch-screen capabilities simplify the ordering process, even for those who may not be tech-savvy. Additionally, the option to switch languages breaks down barriers and ensures inclusivity.
Boosting Sales and Revenue through Quick Service Restaurant
Upselling and Cross-Selling Opportunities

Self-service kiosks are programmed with algorithms that encourage upselling and cross-selling. Suggestions for complementary items or upgrades are automatically displayed during the ordering process, increasing the likelihood of customers adding extras to their meals. This automated approach often results in higher average check sizes compared to traditional cashier interactions.
Promotions and Loyalty Programs

Kiosks can also play a crucial role in promoting special deals, seasonal offers, and loyalty programs. Displaying targeted promotions and rewarding customers for their loyalty through the kiosk interface creates an engaging and rewarding experience, encouraging repeat visits and fostering customer loyalty.
Streamlining the Ordering Process
Enhanced Order Accuracy

Order accuracy is critically important in the QSR industry. Miscommunication between the customer and cashier can lead to incorrect orders, which not only frustrates customers but also incurs additional costs for the restaurant. Self-service kiosks eliminate this risk by allowing customers to input their orders directly, ensuring that the precise details of their requests are captured without error.
Real-Time Modifications

Self-service kiosks enable customers to make real-time modifications to their orders, such as changing ingredients, adjusting portion sizes, or altering cooking preferences. This flexibility ensures that orders are tailored to each customer's liking, enhancing their overall dining experience.
Improving Data Collection and Insights
Detailed Customer Insights

Self-service kiosks are a valuable tool for collecting detailed customer data. Information such as order history, preferences, and buying patterns can be captured and analyzed to gain valuable insights into customer behavior. These insights can help QSRs make data-driven decisions regarding menu offerings, marketing strategies, and operational improvements.
Inventory Management

By integrating self-service kiosks with inventory management systems, QSRs can track real-time sales data and adjust stock levels accordingly. This integration helps prevent stockouts, reduce waste, and ensure that popular items are always available, thereby improving overall operational efficiency.
Meeting Health and Safety Standards
Contactless Ordering and Payment

In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, contactless solutions have become increasingly important. Self-service kiosks offer a safer alternative to traditional ordering methods by minimizing physical contact between customers and staff. Many kiosks also support contactless payment options, further reducing the risk of virus transmission and promoting a safer dining environment.
Hygiene and Sanitation

Regular cleaning and sanitization of self-service kiosks can ensure that they remain safe for customer use. High-touch areas can be coated with antimicrobial films, and hand sanitizing stations can be placed nearby to encourage customer hygiene. Implementing these measures helps maintain a clean and safe environment for all customers.
Final Thoughts

Self-service kiosks are revolutionizing the quick service restaurant industry by enhancing operational efficiency, improving the customer experience, boosting sales, and providing valuable data insights. The integration of these kiosks into QSR models represents a forward-thinking approach to meeting the evolving needs and expectations of today's customers.

As the industry continues to adapt and innovate, self-service kiosks will undoubtedly play a pivotal role in shaping the future of quick service restaurants. Adopting this technology is not just a trend but a strategic move to stay competitive and deliver exceptional service in a fast-paced world.
Ready to transform your QSR with self-service kiosks? Book a product demo today and discover how this innovative technology can elevate your customer experience and streamline your operations.

body.text: The digital age has revolutionized the way we order food, making online ordering systems a common feature for many restaurants. While these platforms offer convenience and accessibility to customers, it's crucial for restaurant owners to carefully assess whether they're a wise investment or a potential financial burden.

In this comprehensive guide, we'll delve into the advantages and disadvantages of online ordering systems, exploring factors such as cost, implementation, customer experience, and impact on operations.

By understanding the nuances of these systems, you'll be equipped to make an informed decision that aligns with your restaurant's unique needs and goals. Whether you're a seasoned restaurateur or just starting out, this guide will provide valuable insights to help you navigate the world of online ordering and determine if it's the right fit for your business.
The Upsides: Why Online Ordering Systems Are So Tempting

1. Increased Convenience: Let's face it, we're all a bit addicted to convenience. Online ordering systems tap into that desire, offering customers a seamless way to browse menus, customize orders, and pay without leaving their couch. This convenience factor can significantly broaden your customer base.

2. Higher Order Values: Studies show that customers tend to spend more when ordering online compared to in-person or over the phone. Why? Because online systems make it easy to add extras, explore the full menu, and avoid the pressure of a line forming behind them.

3. Reduced Labor Costs: Handling phone orders and in-person payments takes up staff time. With online ordering, customers do the work themselves, freeing up your staff to focus on food preparation and customer service. This can lead to significant savings on labor costs.

4. Data Insights: Online ordering systems collect valuable data on customer preferences, popular items, and ordering patterns. This information is gold for menu optimization, marketing campaigns, and even predicting future trends.

5. 24/7 Availability: Your virtual doors never close. Online ordering allows you to take orders around the clock, even when your physical restaurant is closed. This expands your reach and opens up new revenue streams, particularly during late-night cravings or busy workdays.
The Downsides: The Hidden Costs and Challenges

1. Commission Fees: Most online ordering platforms charge commission fees, typically a percentage of each order. These fees can eat into your profits, especially for smaller restaurants with lower margins. The good thing is, eatOS online ordering system has no third-party commission protocol.

2. Loss of Control: When you partner with a third-party platform, you give up some control over your brand and customer relationships. You're also subject to their rules and policies, which may not always align with your business goals.

3. Technical Glitches: Technology isn't perfect. System crashes, bugs, or payment processing issues can lead to frustrated customers and lost orders. Make sure the platform you choose has reliable customer support and a good track record.

4. Menu Management Headaches: Keeping your online menu updated and accurate can be a challenge, especially if you have a large menu or frequent changes. Mistakes can lead to unhappy customers and additional work for your staff.

5. Customer Expectations: Online ordering sets a high bar for speed and convenience. Customers expect their food fast, and any delays or issues can quickly turn them off. Make sure you have the infrastructure in place to handle the increased demand.
Making the Right Choice: Questions to Ask Yourself

items: Do I need a third-party platform, or can I build my own? Building your own system gives you more control but requires technical expertise and a larger upfront investment.
How will I handle the increased demand? Do you have enough staff, kitchen capacity, and delivery drivers to meet the expected influx of orders?
What's my plan for marketing and promoting my online ordering? Don't just set it and forget it. Actively promote your online ordering options to attract new customers and encourage repeat business.

body.text: The Verdict: It's All About Finding the Right Balance
Online ordering systems can be a powerful tool for boosting sales and reaching new customers. But they come with costs and challenges that need careful consideration.
Pro Tip: If you're unsure, start small. Try partnering with one platform or limit your online ordering hours to test the waters and assess the impact on your business.
By weighing the pros and cons and choosing a platform that aligns with your specific needs, you can harness the power of online ordering to grow your restaurant and stay ahead of the curve.

title: Paradero Todos Santos Launches New Culinary Experience: Tenoch
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: The Baja California Peninsula's premier wellness-focused, high-end hotel experience, Paradero Todos Santos, is now home to TENOCH, a captivating restaurant concept that features modern Mexican cuisine with an...

body.text: The Baja California Peninsula's premier wellness-focused, high-end hotel experience, Paradero Todos Santos, is now home to TENOCH, a captivating restaurant concept that features modern Mexican cuisine with an international flair, created by Chef Eduardo Rios. Drawing inspiration from La Gran Tenochtitlan, the ancient Aztec city buried beneath Mexico City, the reimagined culinary concept has taken over the property's existing restaurant space in the center.

The name of the restaurant "TENOCH" refers to the edible flower that grows on the Cacti. This term was once used to refer to the Mexica's ancient leaders. It delves deep into the remarkable culinary scene of Baja California. It also incorporates a wide range of regional methods and ingredients that each dish benefits from. The Paradero on-site garden is still conveniently close to the alfresco dining area. It provides the kitchen with fresh herbs and vegetables, with an emphasis on in-season items like tomatoes, arugula, eggplant, strawberries, papaya, and more.
Honoring Mexican Heritage

Tenoch pays homage to Mexico's vibrant culinary traditions while infusing them with contemporary sophistication. The restaurant is named after the legendary Aztec ruler who founded Tenochtitlan. The concept of the restaurant is centered on a profound reverence for local ingredients, traditional cooking techniques, and the craft of culinary storytelling. Tenoch has appointed Chef Ricardo Muñoz Zurita, a well-known figure in Mexican cuisine, as its culinary director. Known for his commitment to maintaining family recipes and proficiency in classic Mexican cooking, Chef Muñoz Zurita offers a superfluity of enthusiasm and experience to try.
A Culinary Philosophy and Menu

Dedication to sustainability and farm-to-table philosophy is the core of the culinary philosophy of Tenoch. To ensure that every dish that they serve is flavorful, fresh, and an authentic representation of the area, all the ingredients used are sourced from local farmers, fishers, and artisans. High-quality ingredients are sourced from the culinary team at Tenoch. They keep these points in mind while choosing organic produce, seafood, and free-range meat.

Tenoch's menu takes diners on a culinary tour of the various regions of Mexico. Expect a wide range of dishes that highlight the distinct flavors and cooking methods of Puebla, Yucatán, Oaxaca, and other regions. The restaurant's signature dishes are ceviche de camarón, which consists of succulent shrimp marinated in lime juice, cilantro, and a hint of habanero; cochinita pibil, a slow-roasted pork dish wrapped in banana leaves and marinated in achiote; and mole negro, a rich and complex sauce made with over thirty ingredients.

Every day, the best proteins are procured from nearby farmers and fishers who specialize in native Mexican species. This results in a carefully chosen menu featuring dishes like giant prawns and chocolate clams, as well as boeuf bourguignon and carbonara. To prepare specialty tacos like the marinated beef tongue and soft shell crab, Chef Rios and his crew still make their cherished heirloom corn tortillas in the clay oven. Regarding the drink menu, skilled mixologists create sophisticated, minimally designed drinks with a range of proofs from zero to high. Other highlights of the menu are:
• Chingon Oysters \| New York Steak, Ponzu, Ikura
• Zarandeado Shrimps \| Chile Toreado Mayo, Crispy Garlic, Togarashi
• Octopus Tlayuda \| Acuyo Beans, Cherry Salad
• Lychee Panna Cotta \| Mango Mousse, Goat Cheese

Chef Eduardo Rios is concentrating on using functional techniques, a skill he has honed throughout his culinary career, at TENOCH to elevate dining beyond the conventional recipe method and provide patrons with flavors that are directly sourced from the earth. To highlight the seasonality, the menu served for breakfast, lunch, and dinner changes from time to time.
Innovative Dining Spaces

To improve the whole culinary experience at Tenoch, they offer a plethora of eating areas. They have set up the main dining areas with handcrafted decor that symbolizes the artistic past of Mexico. This in turn creates a cozy yet elegant atmosphere. An open kitchen brings excitement and transparency to the dining experience by letting guests watch the culinary team in action. Tenoch offers private dining rooms for special occasions and small groups, ideal for those looking for a more personal experience.

The beginning of an exciting new era is finally here with the opening of Tenoch at Paradero Todos Santos. Visitors will get a dining experience that is rich in cultural legacy with a touch of modern culinary artistry.

Customer Insights: Understanding customer behavior through data can inform marketing strategies and promotional campaigns. Knowing peak dining times, preferred dishes, and spending patterns can help tailor your offerings to meet customer demand.

title: Essential Security and Privacy for Tableside Ordering System
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Tableside ordering systems are the hottest ticket to hit restaurants since bottomless mimosas, okay, maybe not that hot, but close. Allowing customers to peruse menus, customize orders, and even pay their bills, all...

body.text: Tableside ordering systems are the hottest ticket to hit restaurants since bottomless mimosas, okay, maybe not that hot, but close. Allowing customers to peruse menus, customize orders, and even pay their bills, all with a tap on a sleek tablet. It's like having a personal waiter at your very beck and call, except way more tech-savvy, and hopefully less prone to forgetting your extra side of fries.

With much convenience comes much responsibility in terms of security and privacy. After all, you quite definitely don't want a customer's financial information or dietary restrictions to end up on the internet faster than you can say "scallion pancake." So, before you ditch the paper menus for a fleet of tablets, let's bust a move on some key security and privacy considerations for your tableside order systems.
Don't Let Your Data Get Hacked: Security on the Dance Floor
Think of your tableside ordering system as a high-stakes dance competition. Your data is the trophy, and hackers are only those rivals trying to steal it. Here's how you ensure they never win:
Encryption is Your Best Friend
Keep Those Updates Coming

Technology is a lot like a constantly updated dance routine. New security threats are always coming up. That's why you have to keep your tableside order system software up to date. Most of the good people out there who provide this kind of tech do auto-updates, but it doesn't really hurt to check on your own either.
Password Power

Weak passwords are the Macarena of cybersecurity: everybody remembers them, and they're no more useful than a wet napkin. Enforce robust and formidable password policies for your staff who will be accessing the system. Think long, complex combinations that would make even the most skilled hacker dizzy.
Privacy Matters: Keeping Your Customers in the Loop

Security is important; however, it need not be at the expense of privacy. Your customers give you private information. It is important to be very open regarding how personal data will be used and protected. Make your customers feel confident and groovy with these tips:
Privacy Policy Cha Cha Cha

In that case, have an express and succinct privacy policy showing what data you collect from customers through the tableside order system, how you make use of the information, and whom you share it with. Ensure easy accessibility to it on your website and within the ordering app itself. Nobody is fond of hidden surprises, least of all where their data is involved.
Opt-in for the Win

Empower your customers with control over their information. Allow them to opt in, or even better, to opt out of receiving marketing emails or promotional offers through the tableside order system about upcoming salsa dance lessons. No one likes to think that they are being spammed with unnecessary emails unless, of course, they had opted in for them.
Minimisation Mambo

Collect only what is necessary for the ordering system to work. There is no reason to have a record of a customer's entire life story just because he ordered a burger and fries. The less data you collect, the less there is to potentially compromise.
Train Your Crew

Want to teach your staff why data privacy in customer/staff information handling is important and the steps involved in case of a breach? Think about it as some kind of team dance, the members have to work together to avoid missteps.
Security and Privacy: The Powerful Pair

Consider the safety and privacy of the application first, so it's a recipe for success, not a recipe for disaster. Customers have confidence once they learn that all their information is safe and secure within this system. The Surge of Online Ordering

Online food ordering has increased tremendously during the past few years. The revenue in the Online Food Delivery market is forecasted to reach US$1.20tn in 2024. It is expected to exhibit a compound annual growth rate (CAGR 2024-2029) of 9.04%, resulting in a projected market volume of US$1.85tn by 2029.

It is obvious why customers would prefer ordering from their smartphones with the ease of ordering and numerous options in delivery services. However, along with this surge comes some new challenges restaurant owners are now forced to answer.
Challenges of Online Ordering
1\. Integration With Existing Systems

This will, however, be one of the major challenges: getting this online ordering platform to be fully seamless with your current point-of-sale system. Important in terms of ease, but also that manual entry errors do not occur. Depending upon how complex the technical integrations would need to be of your current implementation, the challenge mostly is to be able to integrate both without the necessity for investment in new software or services.
2\. Delivery logistics

The other challenge is the logistics associated with delivery. It becomes cumbersome to maintain food quality to deliver on time and manage the delivery people. Outsourcing with third-party delivery services takes partial pressure off but adds other issues: working in tandem with their delivery schedules and high commission fees.
3\. Managing Food Quality

One of the challenging things is ensuring food reaches the customer in perfect condition. The quality of the food delivered depends on temperature control, type of packaging, and transit times. One has to invest in high-quality packaging and delivery processes for customer satisfaction.
4\. Increased Order Volume Handling

Online ordering often results in sudden spikes in volume, particularly during peak hours. This usually overwhelms the kitchen, and as a result, the wait time increases, mistakes are made, and the service loses quality. Proper scaling of your operations is paramount in handling increased demand.
5\. Customer Expectations

They hope for everything at present with not even a single second of glitches. So, any lag, any delay, or any kind of flaw can turn things seriously for the worst in terms of the reviews. That's why one must make sure that they deliver a frictionless user experience on an online ordering platform to meet and rise above the expectations of their customers.
Opportunities for Online Ordering
1\. Increased Reach and Sales

One of the biggest opportunities is the ability to capture more eyeballs. Ordering online will help you reach out to people who love to stay at home and eat, thus giving you a broader market. Of course, this will retrieve added money and, ultimately, growth.
2\. Insights from Data

With the help of online ordering platforms, you will be able to analyze the information on customer preferences, order patterns, and peak times. This data-based analysis will help you know more about customer behavior, which will be helpful in the personalized design of your menu items, achieving optimization in operations, and focused marketing strategies.
3\. Enhanced Customer Engagement

Most online ordering systems come with features such as loyalty programs, personalized promotions, and feedback mechanisms. These will help enhance customer engagement, foster loyalty, and encourage repurchase.
4\. Operations Management

When properly integrated, online ordering supports operations. Automated order processing will reduce human errors, and real-time inventory updates contribute to better management of stock levels. This improvement can thus free staff to focus on achieving in-house excellence in service.
5\. Brand Affiliation and Marketing
Brand affiliation and marketing are packed in most of the online ordering platforms. Exploiting through them will increase the restaurant's online presence and bring in new customers.
Best Practices for Implementation of Online Ordering
1\. Choosing the Right Platform

Choosing the right online ordering platform is going to be the most important thing. Look for solutions that easily integrate with current systems, have robust features, and have strong customer support.
2\. Optimize Your Menu for Delivery

Not every menu item travels well or holds up during delivery. Be diligent about the items on your menu and support with a separate delivery menu, if necessary. Good descriptions and attractive photographs of food items help to enhance the online ordering experience.
3\. Invest in Quality Packaging

Invest in high-quality packaging that maintains the temperature and integrity of your food. You can also use green packaging that might be more appealing to environmentally conscious consumers. Proper packaging, use ensures the best state in which your food can arrive at your client's doorstep, which will reflect well on your brand.
4\. Train Your Staff

Make sure that your staff can operate the Online Ordering System. Proper training is necessary for added volume in the kitchen, as well as for coordination with delivery drivers by front-of-house staff. Clear protocols and open lines of communication can help steer clear of bottlenecks and errors.
5\. Market Your Online Ordering System

Promote the availability of your online ordering system through your social media, website, and in-store displays. Offering incentives such as discounts for first-time online orders can encourage customers to try out your service.
Conclusion: Embrace the Digital Future

The rise of online food ordering brings along with it challenges and opportunities for restaurant operators. Face these challenges and take up the opportunities with your improving operations, maximizing revenue, and delivering great customer experiences.

title: AI in Food Industry: Latest Tech Advancements - eatOS
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Artificial Intelligence (AI) isn't just about self-driving cars or chatbots anymore. It's revolutionizing industries we might not expect, including the food industry. From the way we grow crops to how we order takeout,...

body.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI) isn't just about self-driving cars or chatbots anymore. It's revolutionizing industries we might not expect, including the food industry. From the way we grow crops to how we order takeout, AI is making its presence known. Let's dive into some of the most fascinating ways this technology is transforming how we produce and consume food.
AI in the Food Industry
Smarter Farming: AI in Agriculture
The Challenge: Growing enough food to feed a growing population while dealing with unpredictable weather patterns and limited resources is a massive challenge.

The AI Solution: AI-powered tools are helping farmers make data-driven decisions. Drones with image recognition software can monitor crops, spotting pests or diseases before they become widespread. Machine learning algorithms analyze soil data and weather patterns to optimize irrigation and fertilizer use. The result? More efficient farming practices that yield larger, healthier crops.
Robots in the Kitchen: Automating Food Preparation
The Challenge: Restaurants and food processing facilities face labor shortages and the need to maintain consistent quality in their food.

The AI Solution: Robots are stepping into the kitchen. They can perform repetitive tasks like chopping vegetables, flipping burgers, or even making sushi rolls. AI-powered machines are also being used to sort and package food, ensuring quality control and reducing waste.
Personalized Dining Experiences: AI and Customer Preferences
The Challenge: Every diner is unique. How do restaurants cater to individual tastes and dietary restrictions?

The AI Solution: Imagine a restaurant that knows your favorite dishes and can recommend new ones you might enjoy. AI-powered apps and platforms can analyze customer data to create personalized menus, suggest pairings, and even predict future cravings. This isn't just about convenience; it's about a dining experience that truly feels tailored to you.
Streamlining the Supply Chain: AI's Logistics Advantage
The Challenge: Getting food from farm to fork is a complex process involving multiple steps and a lot of coordination.

The AI Solution: AI is helping to optimize the entire food supply chain. It can predict demand for specific products, ensuring that stores are stocked with the right items at the right time. AI-powered logistics systems can even choose the most efficient routes for delivery trucks, reducing transportation costs and food waste.
Food Safety and Traceability: AI as a Watchdog
The Challenge: Foodborne illnesses are a serious concern. How do we trace the source of contamination and prevent outbreaks?

The AI Solution: AI-powered sensors can monitor food temperatures throughout the supply chain, alerting producers and distributors to any potential problems. Blockchain technology, often associated with cryptocurrencies, is also being used to create transparent records of where food has been and how it's been handled, making it easier to track and recall products if necessary.
What's Next on the AI Menu?

The future of AI in the food industry is full of possibilities. We might see AI-powered chefs creating entirely new dishes based on our individual preferences. Smart kitchens could automate even more of the cooking process, making meal prep a breeze. AI could even play a role in developing healthier and more sustainable food products.
A Few Bytes of Caution

While AI offers exciting opportunities, it's important to consider potential challenges. There are concerns about job displacement as automation becomes more widespread. We also need to ensure that AI systems are transparent and accountable, especially when it comes to food safety.
Conclusion:

The rise of AI in the food industry is a delicious example of how technology can transform even the most traditional of industries. From farm to fork, AI is poised to make our food systems more efficient, sustainable, and personalized. As we embrace these advancements, let's not forget to savor the human touch that makes food so special. After all, the best meals are often those shared with friends and family, creating memories that no AI can replicate.

title: When to Promote for the Fall and Winter Holidays
author: eatOS Staff
excerpt: Marketing your restaurant is delicate. When it comes to the major holidays that happen in the autumn and winter, you have to get a head start to catch customers’ attention. But starting too early risks annoying them...

body.text: Marketing your restaurant is delicate. When it comes to the major holidays that happen in the autumn and winter, you have to get a head start to catch customers’ attention. But starting too early risks annoying them with out-of-season ads that won’t stick in their heads come showtime. That’s a waste of money, too. Some customers start holiday shopping in October, well before Black Friday, so that’s not the marker for when to promote new sales either.
When should your restaurant start marketing for the late holidays?
Ready for the Big Holidays?
Photo by David Menidrey on Unsplash
Halloween

The best time to start announcing your spooky sales is September, but not too soon. Customers start getting in the Halloween spirit about a month prior. More and more people get excited the closer it gets to the day.

When it comes to the promotions themselves, restaurants are encouraged to get creative. You don’t have to invent all-new menus to get in the Halloween spirit either. Use your imagination to use what you already have on hand. Add orange dye and bat-themed decorations, for example, or change the drinks to have more festive names. Just these little touches add up to a fun Halloween atmosphere when the sales begin.
Thanksgiving

It’s optimal to start advertising three weeks before Thanksgiving. Stay mindful that Halloween just passed. Just afterwards is around when social media platforms notice an uptick in clicks for relevant Turkey Day buzzwords, so do what you can to end up in those search results. Joining Google My Business is a great way to get more online traffic to your webpages and socials, where you then have the opportunity to convert clicks to sales (or at least reservations that portends profit). As soon as Halloween ends, overhaul the decorations for Thanksgiving ASAP.
Christmas

There’s a reason that promos for the December holidays often coincide with Thanksgiving. Start rolling out the Christmas decor in mid-November, because that’s when the customers will start looking for deals. If you have a webstore, for example, where you may sell branded t-shirts and mugs, you’ll have enough time to advertise your Black Friday prices. Then customers have plenty of time to get excited for it, too.

As one of the major holidays, Christmas sales don’t end when the promotions do, or even on Christmas itself. Often, businesses keep them going all the way through New Year. Plenty of people shop after the holidays because of next-day price drops, and others celebrate with different friends when they all have time. Keep the promotions going and the sales will stay steady, too.
Photo by Annie Spratt on Unsplash
What Happens if You Promote Too Late?

The fall and winter holidays are traditionally quite profitable. If you don’t promote early enough in the year, you may not have enough stock to meet all the demand when hungry customers all pour in at once. The rush could also result in slower service which hurts customer satisfaction, table turns and servers’ tips. Also, waiting to promote your restaurant means wasting time that could be pulling in profit from these deals. Start early and the crowd will trickle in, which is easier for staff to handle, provides a better overall experience and gives you the most possible benefits from these major holidays.

Still, these are simply guidelines. What works best for your restaurant isn’t a one-size-fits-all thing. For example, men are more likely to begin shopping later than women. This is just one small statistic, but it demonstrates that your target demographic heavily affects spending habits and what promotions will do well. More useful than conforming to the “average,” rely on smart Point of Sale systems to generate real-time reports about sales trends and consumer habits. Set your restaurant on the right long-term track.

body.text: The restaurant industry continuously evolves, integrating technology to enhance customer experience and streamline operations. One significant innovation gaining traction is the use of self-service kiosks. If you're a restaurant owner or manager looking to boost sales and improve efficiency, this guide will help you understand the benefits of self-service kiosks and offer strategies for successful implementation.
Understanding the Benefits of Self-Service Kiosks
Before diving into strategies, let’s highlight why self-service kiosks can be game changers for your restaurant.

1. Enhanced Customer Experience: Customers enjoy the convenience and speed of self-service kiosks. They can browse the menu at their own pace, customize their orders, and pay quickly without waiting in lines.
2. Increased Order Accuracy: By allowing customers to input their orders directly, kiosks reduce the chances of human error, ensuring that every order is correct and tailored to customer preferences.
3. Higher Average Check Sizes: Kiosks can effectively upsell and cross-sell by suggesting add-ons, combos, and premium items, typically resulting in higher average order values.
4. Operational Efficiency: With kiosks handling the order-taking process, staff can focus on food preparation and customer service, ultimately speeding up service and reducing wait times.
Strategies for Successfully Implementing Self-Service Kiosks
Now that you understand the benefits, let’s explore the strategies you can use to ensure your self-service kiosks are a success.
1\. Choose the Right Kiosk System
Not all self-service kiosks are created equal. Here are some key factors to consider when choosing a kiosk system:

items: User-Friendly Interface: Ensure the software is intuitive and easy for customers to navigate.
Customization: Look for solutions that allow you to customize the interface to reflect your brand and menu offerings.
Integration: Your kiosk system should seamlessly integrate with your existing point-of-sale (POS) system and kitchen display systems (KDS).
Support and Maintenance: Opt for a provider that offers robust customer support and regular software updates.

body.text: 2\. Optimize Menu Design
The way you present your menu on the kiosks can significantly impact sales. Here’s how to make it appealing:

items: High-Quality Images: Use appetizing, high-resolution images for each menu item.
Clear Descriptions: Provide clear and concise descriptions of each dish, highlighting key ingredients and potential allergens.
Highlight Specials: Feature daily specials, combos, and high-margin items prominently.
Customization Options: Allow easy customization for items, such as adding extra toppings or sides, to enhance the ordering experience.

body.text: 3\. Encourage Upselling and Cross-Selling
Leverage the technology to increase your average check size by:

items: Suggestive Selling: Program the kiosk to suggest complementary items or upgrades during the ordering process. For example, if someone orders a burger, the kiosk could suggest adding fries and a drink.
Combo Deals: Highlight combo deals and meal bundles that offer value for money while increasing the overall sale.
Limited-Time Offers: Promote limited-time offers and seasonal items to create a sense of urgency.

body.text: 4\. Streamline the Ordering Process
A streamlined ordering process enhances customer satisfaction and efficiency:

items: Simple Navigation: Organize the menu logically with categorized sections (e.g., appetizers, mains, desserts).
Quick Pay Options: Integrate multiple payment options, including credit cards, mobile wallets, and loyalty points, for a seamless checkout experience.
Order Tracking: Provide real-time order tracking updates to keep customers informed about their order status.

body.text: 5\. Promote the Kiosks to Customers
Let your customers know about the new kiosks and why they should use them:

items: In-Store Signage: Use eye-catching signs and digital displays to draw attention to the kiosks.
Staff Recommendations: Train staff to guide customers to the kiosks and assist them with their first use.
Social Media and Marketing: Announce the kiosks on your social media platforms, website, and email newsletters, highlighting their benefits.

body.text: 6\. Train Your Staff
Your team plays a crucial role in the successful implementation of self-service kiosks:

items: Initial Training: Conduct comprehensive training sessions to familiarize staff with the kiosk system and its operations.
Ongoing Support: Provide ongoing training and support to ensure staff can troubleshoot minor issues and assist customers as needed.
Customer Assistance: Encourage staff to proactively offer help to customers who might be hesitant or unfamiliar with using kiosks.

body.text: 7\. Monitor Performance and Gather Feedback
Continuous improvement is key to the success of any new technology:

items: Analytics and Reports: Use the kiosk system’s reporting features to track sales, popular items, and customer behavior.
Customer Feedback: Collect feedback directly from customers about their kiosk experience. A simple survey at the end of the transaction can provide valuable insights.
Make Adjustments: Regularly review performance reports and customer feedback to make necessary adjustments to the kiosk setup, menu, or promotional strategies.

body.text: 8\. Create a Seamless Omnichannel Experience
Ensure that your self-service kiosks complement other ordering channels:

items: Unified Menu: Maintain consistency across kiosks, online ordering platforms, and in-store menus to avoid confusion.
Integrated Loyalty Programs: Allow customers to earn and redeem loyalty points seamlessly, regardless of whether they order via kiosk, online, or at the counter.
Consistent Branding: Ensure your brand’s look and feel are consistent across all channels to provide a cohesive customer experience.

Implementing self-service kiosks in your restaurant can significantly boost sales, enhance customer experience, and streamline operations. By choosing the right kiosk system, optimizing your menu design, encouraging upselling, and promoting the kiosks, you can make the most of this innovative technology. With these strategies in place, you’ll be well on your way to reaping the benefits of self-service kiosks and driving success in your restaurant.
